existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `TestReport` appears to be removed from R6 core, producing a hard R4-to-R6 validation and code-generation break. The top migration concerns are unknown resource type validation failures, loss of generated classes/endpoints/search support, and no obvious lossless standard target for TestScript execution-result semantics. The main uncertainty is the official HL7 rationale and recommended replacement path.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is resource-retirement work rather than element-level remodeling. Systems should inventory stored `TestReport` instances, generated model classes, validators, search endpoints, and integrations that exchange TestScript execution reports. A safe migration will usually preserve the R4 payload as legacy content or map to an implementation-specific/reporting artifact with an explicit profile; mapping to unrelated `DiagnosticReport` or `MeasureReport` resources should not be assumed without domain review.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R6 ballot package lacks `TestReport`: the assigned file is absent, the R6 package index has no TestReport entries, and targeted filename/code searches found no core TestReport StructureDefinition. Confidence is lower on the intended replacement strategy because no official diff, narrative page, or change-note evidence was available locally.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
TestReport has a resource-identity break: TestReport resource is absent from the R6 core package. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 91/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
